title: Adaptive runbook selector using trace-pattern classifiers for PagerDuty + Slack enrichment
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: On-call responders spend time choosing or editing runbooks for each PagerDuty trigger. For recurring failure modes we can reduce mean time to mitigation by recommending the most relevant runbook and pre-populating Slack quick-actions with evidence (trace snippets, top spans, latency slices).

This ticket is to build an adaptive runbook selector service that: 1) consumes PagerDuty alerts + linked trace snippets, 2) classifies the alert into a small set of runbook candidates using lightweight trace-pattern classifiers and signal heuristics, 3) enriches the PD payload and Slack incident thread with the top runbook link, short rationale (e.g., "tail latency spike on checkout-service => DB timeouts"), and one-click mitigation actions (roll back, throttle, failover).

Goals: reduce manual runbook selection, improve first-action correctness, and shorten incident context-gathering time. The classifier will be hybrid: heuristics ruleset + a small supervised model trained on historical incidents and postmortem labels. Fallbacks: if classifier confidence < threshold, present top-3 suggestions without pre-populating actions. Privacy: PII/redacted spans only; follow Private deployment opt-outs for on-prem customers.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype service ingests PD webhook and attached trace snippet within 2s in staging
Top-1 suggested runbook matches postmortem label >= 70% on historical eval set (sample of 600 incidents)
Slack incident thread shows runbook card + rationale + 2 quick actions when confidence >= 0.8
Telemetry dashboard captures suggestion_accuracy, suggestion_latency, and action_click_rate
Feature has a kill-switch in the Console per-tenant and honors Private deployment redaction settings
implementation_notes: Spike outcome: lightweight TF-IDF + small catboost on span-signatures gave 0.72 F1 in local eval (not yet validated out-of-time)
We will reuse trace-snippet extractor from ENG-27105 and canonicalize span names using the runtime-kv mapping
Security: mark model artifacts for review by security; do not send full traces to hosted inference for Private customers. See security checklist in doc.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (spike): evaluate classifier on labeled incidents; produce offline metrics (Mar week 1)
Phase 1 (canary): enable suggestions for 10% of hosted tenants with PD -> Slack flow; collect metrics and manual QA (Mar week 3)
Phase 2: enable quick-actions for tenants with >0.8 model confidence and with security_review_required=false (Apr week 1)
Phase 3: gradual ramp to 25% then 100% with rollback monitor and automated disable on error budget burn (Apr)
Post-launch: runbook suggestion accuracy review every 2 weeks and add new labeled incidents to training set
